rubric.result: The objective promises three things and each has production lines behind it in SpecFreezePanel.tsx. (a) 'the cabin shows the yardstick's failures': the draft branch renders the BLOCKED paragraph and a <ul> of findings, each label built by findingLabel (lines 24-25, 261-271 of the diff), which appends ', linea <line>: <detail>' only when the finding carries a line — the hypothesis-absent finding of the mother has line null and detail null and renders the bare label instead of 'undefined'. (b) 'a button that refuses while any remains': isDisabled = findings.length > 0 || gateKey === null, passed to Button's disabled. (c) 'once frozen — the date, the pull request and that the groom waits for its merge': the frozen branch renders `${FROZEN} ${frozen.on}.`, the anchor `${PULL_REQUEST} #${number}` href'd to the pull request url when it is not null, and WAITING. The freeze itself goes through SpecFreezeClient.freeze(gateKey), which is the real client committed by task 11. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The TDD line asks for it('refuses the freeze while a clarification marker remains and shows the line the backend gave') — with SpecFreezeMother.draftWithMarker() the button disabled and the finding's line and raw text on screen. The diff's first test is that name verbatim, stubs fetch with draftWithMarker().body, and asserts findByText('Marcador de clarificacion sin resolver, linea 42: [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: which button?]') plus getByRole('button', {name:'Congelar el spec'}) toBeDisabled(). I checked the input against the mother that task 11 actually committed: MARKER_FINDING is {code:'clarification-marker', line:42, detail:'[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: which button?]'}, so 42 and the raw marker text are the backend's own values travelling through the real client, not values retyped in the test. Same assertion, same input, same expected value. The boundary pair the line also asks for is present as 'lets the freeze go once no finding remains' over draftReady(), asserting the same button toBeEnabled().

The Contract block declares nine constants with literal values; all nine appear in SpecFreezePanel.tsx character for character, including the middle dot in HEADING, the angle quotes in the two Hipotesis labels, the three finding codes as keys and the trailing full stops of ONLY_FROM_THE_PAGE and WAITING. The prose contract is met too: no props, reads useSpecFreeze, connecting/none/no-spec/unavailable render null, draft renders Panel heading={HEADING} with the findings list and the button, the button disabled while findings.length > 0 or key === null, ONLY_FROM_THE_PAGE rendered when there is no key, freeze called with the key, a refusal rendered as Banner type="error" role="alert" with the detail untranslated (Banner puts role from ...rest after its own default, so role="alert" wins — verified in system-ui/banner/Banner.tsx line 52), the frozen text/anchor/WAITING triple, and BEM classes under spec-freeze-panel__. One constant beyond the block: UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE = 'No se pudo contactar con el backend', for FreezeAskOutcome's third member; it is the same constant with the same value as the named exemplar ImplementPlanAction.tsx line 9. I record it here rather than as a contract deviation because the block adds constants, it does not forbid them, and the member it serves is real (client.ts returns backend-unreachable when fetch throws or the body is unreadable).

Six rows bear on this diff and each is implemented with the value it states. D-6 (the gate is an act of the app, a button the program answers for): the freeze is a Button whose onClick posts, not a line an agent writes. D-22 (no session can trigger the gate; the request carries the key): freezeSpec returns early when gateKey is null and otherwise calls SpecFreezeClient.freeze(gateKey), which sends the x-gate-key header; with no key the button stays disabled and ONLY_FROM_THE_PAGE says why. D-23 (after the freeze the app publishes and the groom waits for the merge): WAITING says exactly that, once. D-7 (no merge button anywhere in the cabin, the app never writes to a pull request): the frozen branch contains one <a href> to the pull request and nothing that writes — a link is a read. D-21 (no phase of the page may hide the coordinating session): this component returns null in four phases and a Panel in two; it neither renders nor disables anything of the coordinating session. D-13 (no phase is stored): the sticky `asked` is React state inside one render tree, and the brief's own sentence 'frozen is kept and rendered at once, the poll agreeing next round' is what asks for it; nothing is persisted. The remaining rows (D-1, D-10, D-11, D-16, D-18, D-25) have no subject in a frontend component.

Exemplars: the component matches CoordinatingSessionStatus.tsx (module constants for every Spanish label, `if (read.phase === 'connecting') return null` first, Banner type="error" role="alert") and ImplementPlanAction.tsx (useState<Outcome|null>, the refusal Banner titled with the backend's own detail, the identical UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE). The test file matches ImplementProgress.test.tsx exactly: vi.stubGlobal('fetch') over a mother body, afterEach(vi.unstubAllGlobals), real timers, assertions on rendered text. frontend/README.md and the frontend-engineering skill: no semicolons, single quotes, named export, no export default, absolute imports from src/ with relative only inside the folder, no comments, English identifiers with Spanish only in the labels, BEM under spec-freeze-panel__, descriptive callback name in findings.map((finding, index)) — all held. CLAUDE.md's language rule: the rendered labels are Spanish (product copy, the one exemption), everything else English. defects.md, rule by rule. (1) Closed vocabulary: the panel dispatches over SpecFreezeOutcome and FreezeAskOutcome by `kind`, real closed unions from task 11. Two observations I weighed and did not raise. FINDING is a Record<string,string> indexed by finding.code, whose type is `string` — an unmapped code would render 'undefined'; but the Contract block prescribes `const FINDING: Record<string, string>` verbatim and FreezeFinding.code lives in SpecFreeze.types.ts, which this task's **Files:** does not include, so no diff the implementer could write inside this task narrows it. And `if (read.kind !== 'draft') return null` collapses none/no-spec/unavailable into one negative guard where CoordinatingSessionStatus enumerates them, so a sixth member would render nothing silently; the brief prescribes that exact behaviour for all of them and the failure mode is rendering nothing, so I report it here rather than as a finding. (2) Raw map as the return value of logic: no subject — findingLabel returns a string, the component returns JSX, and FINDING is a label table, not a value crossing two functions. (3) Two fields that have to agree: none, and the opposite is what is written — `frozen` is derived from `asked` and `read` instead of a separate isFrozen flag, absences are `null` (key, pullRequest, line, detail) with no empty string or zero standing in for one. (4) An error named for where it happens: no subject — this diff declares no error type. Delivery: nothing in either yardstick prescribes a shape for shipping a new, not-yet-wired component, and the diff wires nothing into Home (task 13's business), so there is no old path left behind. Boundaries: the only edge crossed is fetch, and it is crossed through task 11's client, not re-opened here. One tension declared, not reported: conventions/style.md's 'No free function at module level' is broken by `const SpecFreezePanel = () => ...` and by `findingLabel`, and this is a new module so the declared-debt exemption does not shelter it — but the remedy contradicts React's own contract and all four component exemplars the plan names (CoordinatingSessionStatus, ImplementPlanAction, ToolsNavbar's metricsDetail, ImplementHistory's formatLocalTime are the same shape), so the defect is in the stack this repo chose, not in this diff. One finding, low.

No subject. The staged diff is 208 insertions and 0 deletions across four files that are all new (mode 100644 from /dev/null); there is not a single `-` line in it, so no pre-existing assertion, case or test was removed, relaxed or rewritten. I also confirmed the other two files of the spec-freeze suite (client.test.ts, useSpecFreeze.test.ts) are untouched by this task's index.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code. The only double in the file is `fetch` — the real external boundary — and everything between it and the screen runs for real: SpecFreezeClient.read/freeze parse the mother's JSON body, useSpecFreeze polls and narrows, SpecFreezePanel renders, and the design system's real Panel, Button and Banner are mounted. The expected strings are not hard-coded twice: 'Marcador de clarificacion sin resolver, linea 42: [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: which button?]' can only appear if findingLabel composes FINDING[code] with the line and detail the wire carried, and `Spec congelado el ${SpecFreezeMother.ON}.` reads the date out of the mother rather than restating it. Revert SpecFreezePanel.tsx and all seven tests fail on a missing module. The disabled/enabled pair is the sharpest evidence: the same component, two mother bodies, opposite outcomes.

The four touched paths are exactly the four **Files:** declares, all four created, and no plan file appears in the diff — there is no amendment to rule on. Inside them, everything traces to a sentence: the CSS declares six classes and every one of them is used by the TSX; the barrel is the one line **Files:** asks for; the test file holds the seven tests **TDD:** and **Tests:** name and nothing else. The one addition no sentence of the task asks for by name is the `backend-unreachable` branch with its UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE. I do not report it: simplicity.md's question — which call breaks without it — has an answer, since client.ts returns that member whenever the POST's fetch throws or its body is unreadable, and without the branch a pressed button would answer with silence; it is also copied from ImplementPlanAction.tsx, an exemplar the plan names. Nothing that **### Out of scope** names by name is touched: no groom, no slices table, no merge, no plugin skill, no start-plan or implement-plan module.

Seven new tests, and the three properties hold for all of them. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no network, no path, no randomness and no sleep — every input is a literal body from SpecFreezeMother, and the two multi-step tests script the answers with mockResolvedValueOnce in order rather than by timing. Isolated: each test stubs its own fetch, afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllGlobals()) removes it, RTL's cleanup unmounts and the hook's effect clears its timer, and nothing is shared between tests or taken for granted from another file. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on rendered output, except the one on the POST, which is the literal payload at the boundary — toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(2, '/spec-freeze', {method:'POST', headers:{'x-gate-key': KEY}}), matching client.ts's fetch(PATH, {method:'POST', headers:{[GATE_KEY_HEADER]: key}}) exactly — and that same test also asserts the three rendered strings, so it is not a call-count test. I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and its testing-anti-patterns.md reference before looking for anything finer, and what I found there is owned by the plan, not by the implementer: four names carry an 'and' that the skill's 'One thing. "and" in name? Split it.' would split, and all four are the plan's own literal text in **TDD:** and **Tests:**. One genuine weakness, also not the implementer's to fix: 'a spec with no hypothesis shows that finding and keeps the button disabled' runs on draftWithMarker(), which carries the marker finding as well, so the disabled half of its name cannot fail for the reason the name gives — the marker alone would disable the button. Its other half has teeth (it pins the line===null branch of findingLabel, the only test that does), and the mother offers no hypothesis-only scenario while frontend/src/__scenarios__/SpecFreezeMother.ts is outside this task's **Files:**. Nothing here rises to the three that block.

findings.what: The one line that decides which of the two frozen sources to render is a nested ternary chaining three outcomes: the answered freeze, the polled frozen read, and null. The frontend-engineering skill the plan lists under 'Rules to obey' bans exactly that chain in its Quick Rules, and asks for the shape the rest of this very file already uses — the early returns on lines 33, 47 and 48. Written as `if (asked?.kind === 'frozen') return frozenPanel(asked)` beside the existing guards, or as a named derivation, the line stops needing to be parsed twice. Style only: the behaviour is right and both frozen sources are covered by the tests.
findings.evidence: const frozen = asked?.kind === 'frozen' ? asked : read.phase === 'read' && read.kind === 'frozen' ? read : null   —  against the skill's rule: "**No `else`** — use early return or separate `if` blocks with inverted conditions."
